title: Target building practitioner registration at risk and make it work across states
action: Review the registration schemes for building designers and engineers so qualification requirements match the risk of the work, use tiered licences for lower-risk tasks, and ensure registrations are recognised automatically in other states.
why: Registration lifts accountability for building defects, but stricter licensing without evidence raises barriers to entry and limits how quickly firms can bring in staff from other states.

evidence.source: Building a skilled and adaptable workforce: Inquiry report
evidence.quote: Australian, state and territory governments should assess whether current regulated qualification requirements for occupations are proportionate to risks, and identify opportunities to streamline qualification requirements or use more modular or tiered licensing systems to target risk.

evidence.source: Housing construction productivity: Can we fix it?
evidence.quote: The lack of empirical evidence supporting licensing design has led to a ramping up of licensing stringency that has increased barriers to entry and is likely leading to considerable inefficiencies in the provision of skills and reduced productivity in the sector.
